question: ap1
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Measure how much information AP-1 carries about past stimuli (from information theory)
ideas.description: Expose cells to several defined stimulus histories, then use single-cell multiome to estimate the mutual information between each history and the cell's present state, with and without conditioning on AP-1 footprint and activity. If AP-1 is the memory, it should account for nearly all of the history information, so conditioning on it should leave almost none.

ideas.title: Compare memory half-life with AP-1 half-lives (from radioactive decay)
ideas.description: Using pulse-chase designs, measure how fast the primed response fades after a single stimulus. Compare that rate with the half-lives of FOS/JUN proteins (e.g., HaloTag pulse-chase) and of AP-1 chromatin occupancy (CUT&Tag time courses). If the memory lasts much longer than both, AP-1 is more likely to start the memory than to store it.

ideas.title: Test whether AP-1 is enough to create memory (from epidemiology's Bradford Hill criteria)
ideas.description: Address sufficiency, a test that observational correlation can't answer. Use a dCas9 fusion, or a chemically induced AP-1 recruitment system, to tether AP-1 at chosen enhancers for a short time without any stimulus, then release it. Afterwards, check whether those loci stay accessible and respond more strongly to a later challenge.

ideas.title: Check whether memory moves between cells or stays on the chromatin (from organ transplantation)
ideas.description: Fuse primed cells with naive cells to form heterokaryons, or move nuclei into enucleated cytoplasts, and use species- or allele-specific readouts. If the memory moves to the naive nucleus, it is carried by a diffusible factor such as AP-1 protein. If it stays with the primed chromatin, it is stored in the chromatin itself (cis).

ideas.title: Test whether stimulus order matters (from path dependence in economics)
ideas.description: Give cells stimulus A then B, or B then A, with matched total exposure, and measure end states and how they later respond to a drug. Then test whether the effect of order disappears when AP-1 is inhibited, or can be predicted from AP-1 footprints left by the first stimulus.
